claim_boundary: selection optimizes model representation size, not relation probability; report all failed candidates, natural relation yield and operation counts; no online speedup inference
controls: for every chosen curve verify P+(-P)=O and its public reduction; control is separate from natural vector yield
distinct_x_candidates: center both finite points; enumerate shifts (-1,0,1)^4 lexicographically on x1,y1,x2,y2, adding shift times p; interpolate A=(f1-f2)/(x1-x2), B=f1-A*x1; reject singular or bad-reduction models
equal_x_exception: when U,V are distinct opposite points with same x, use centered P=(x,y), R=(x,-y), A=-1, B=y^2-x^3+x; count one construction attempt
falsifiers: candidate construction or chosen lift reduction fails
independent replay disagrees with any raw attempt
full_model_score: max numerator or denominator bit length of A,B,x1,y1,x2,y2
generator_law: first x ascending then y ascending whose cofactor multiple has exact prime order q
query_law: first 16 lexicographic ordered distinct offsets with both public U=Q-t1G and V=Q-t2G nonidentity
question: Does a precommitted minimum-model-height two-image lift rule produce selected rational relations on fresh public queries when all candidate curves and vector tests are charged?
selection_rule: choose minimum full-model score among valid candidates, break ties by lexicographic shift; commit the chosen curve and both points before testing any coefficient vector
target_law: w=1+int(SHA256(xedni-height-selected-v1|p|j),16) mod (q-1), j=0..3; independent seed label from parent
